title: Vectomancy architecture research record
claim_boundary: Research-only observations of the Vectomancy repository. This record is non-canonical, review-required, and does not determine promotion.

source.working_tree_observation: Clean at inspection time; source was inspected read-only.
source.provenance: Direct README, documentation, source, and test inspection at the pinned commit. No Vectomancy files were edited.

included: Raster, SVG, text, and video pipelines
Fourier/FFT, spline, RDP, TSP, and Chaikin transformations
Tests that locally exercise these contracts
excluded: General performance claims not measured by the inspected tests
General mathematical correctness or approximation quality
Historical influence, dependency relations, compatibility, or production readiness
Changes to data/systems, relations, API/MCP, migrations, production artifacts, papers, or MTH-0151

evidence.excerpt: The CLI declares image, video (feature-gated), text, and render subcommands; image accepts multiple input paths/directories and mode/format/terms/Chaikin/detail/tolerance/color/GPU/thread controls, while render consumes MathExpressionAST JSON.
evidence.provenance: README and Clap declarations; dispatch rejects a missing subcommand with InvalidInput.
evidence.limitations: This records the declared interface and dispatch code, not every runtime combination or packaging behavior.

evidence.excerpt: PNG/JPG/JPEG/WEBP file or memory input is decoded; the raster path converts to luminance, computes parallel horizontal/vertical Sobel filters, applies Otsu thresholding, performs Zhang-Suen thinning, traces endpoint and remaining components, and optionally averages RGB pixels along each path.
evidence.provenance: Deterministic source inspection of decode_raster_memory and parser dispatch.
evidence.limitations: The code establishes the implemented stages and data flow, not that the extracted paths are complete, topologically correct, or visually optimal.

evidence.excerpt: usvg parses SVG data, recursively visits groups and paths, maps absolute transforms, preserves line/quadratic/cubic/close segments as BezierSegment values, and optionally converts stroke/fill colors; the CLI treats SVG as Segments and routes it to spline/Fourier/Chaikin branches.
evidence.provenance: Source inspection of both the facade parser and workspace SVG crate.
evidence.limitations: Only inspected path-node handling is asserted; unsupported SVG node kinds and renderer behavior are outside this record.

evidence.excerpt: Raster Paths are filtered by min_path_len, simplified with recursive Ramer-Douglas-Peucker using a perpendicular-distance epsilon, then Spline builds cubic/line equations, Fourier computes FFT terms, or Chaikin applies repeated 0.75/0.25 corner cuts while preserving endpoints for open paths.
evidence.provenance: CLI branch code plus math implementations.
evidence.limitations: The source reveals formulas and branch order; it does not prove approximation error bounds or preservation of all geometric properties.

evidence.excerpt: Points become complex samples (x + i*y), rustfft performs a forward FFT, each coefficient becomes amplitude=norm/n, signed frequency, and phase, and terms are amplitude-sorted. Adaptive mode retains the DC term then accumulates non-DC amplitude squared until the configured energy target or term cap; non-adaptive mode filters amplitude <= 0.001 and takes the cap.
evidence.provenance: Facade math implementation and transform crate implementation both inspected; FourierTerm fields are serialized model fields.
evidence.limitations: This is an implementation description, not a claim that the selected terms reconstruct the input accurately or that the energy threshold is a formal approximation guarantee.

evidence.excerpt: For SVG segments, the CLI samples each segment collection at 100 points, orders those points with a KD-tree nearest-neighbor traversal, then runs bounded 2-opt reversal passes before batch FFT. The same sample/TSP preparation is used for the Chaikin SVG branch.
evidence.provenance: CLI branch and TSP source; transform tests assert the simple nearest-neighbor ordering case.
evidence.limitations: The implementation gives a heuristic ordering procedure; no global TSP optimality or single-stroke quality is established.

evidence.excerpt: build_splines emits SplineEquation records with start_t/end_t and four coefficients for each x/y polynomial. Line, quadratic, cubic, and Close segments are handled; simplify rounds each coefficient to four decimal places.
evidence.provenance: Direct source inspection; transform test verifies a MoveTo/LineTo produces one equation.
evidence.limitations: The formulas are recorded as code evidence; tests do not establish numerical error bounds, continuity across arbitrary segment sequences, or exactness after rounding.

evidence.excerpt: The workspace geometry implementation emits Q0=0.75P0+0.25P1 and Q1=0.25P0+0.75P1 per iteration, doubles interior samples per iteration, and handles closed/open paths separately. The facade implementation preserves first and last points for open paths. A geometry test checks one closed-polyline smoothing result.
evidence.provenance: Algorithm source and local unit test.
evidence.limitations: A local test of one case does not establish general mathematical correctness or intended visual smoothness.

evidence.excerpt: Text accepts TTF/OTF bytes and detects WOFF2 for conversion to TTF, scales glyph outlines, applies kerning and letter spacing, interprets escaped newline/carriage-return sequences, ignores controls, inserts fallback glyphs for missing characters, emits Bezier segments, and defaults to text_output.json when no output path is supplied. The CLI integration test runs 'text hello' with the fixture font and asserts a non-empty output file.
evidence.provenance: Text parser, CLI branch, and integration test.
evidence.limitations: The test does not assert output geometry, font coverage, WOFF2 behavior, or rendering fidelity.

evidence.excerpt: FFmpeg selects the best video stream, decodes packets on a spawned thread into a bounded channel of cloned AVFrame wrappers, converts frames to RGB24 with software scaling, and the CLI batches decoded frames with std::thread::scope. Each frame runs raster extraction and the selected math branch; frame outputs are numbered frame_%04d.<ext>.
evidence.provenance: Video crate and CLI video branch.
evidence.limitations: The source describes concurrency and codec calls, not throughput, memory bounds beyond channel capacity, or behavior under all decoder failures.

evidence.excerpt: When output has a video extension, frame outputs are PNGs in a temporary directory and an external ffmpeg command is invoked at 30 fps. GIF uses palettegen/paletteuse; WebM uses libvpx-vp9 and may use yuva420p; other listed containers use libx264/yuv420p. Audio is probed and, when present and not GIF, mapped to AAC with -shortest.
evidence.provenance: CLI command construction and configuration guide.
evidence.limitations: The command construction is evidence of intended invocation; it does not prove ffmpeg availability, codec success, or audio synchronization.

evidence.excerpt: MathExpressionAST is a tagged enum with Fourier{strokes,bounding_box}, Spline{equations,bounding_box}, and Polyline{paths,bounding_box}. ColoredPath serializes color_style under color_rgb. Deserialization accepts solid and current/legacy gradient forms, normalizes non-finite color inputs, sorts gradient stops, and the emitter rejects non-finite coordinates, coefficients, terms, colors, and invalid bounding boxes/interval ordering.
evidence.provenance: Model and emitter source inspection; emitter validation is called before JSON/template/native output.
evidence.limitations: Validation is a serialization/output boundary check; it is not a semantic validator of the geometry or math.

evidence.excerpt: JSON output is pretty-printed AST. Script outputs serialize selected AST data to JSON, compress it with zlib, and Base64-encode it. Python decodes the payload and evaluates Fourier cosine/sine sums, spline polynomials, or polylines; HTML uses Canvas; Desmos emits parametric expressions and loads expressions in batches of 50. SVG is a separate emitter path.
evidence.provenance: Exporter, emitter, and templates; emitter test decodes the zlib/Base64 payload and checks the original JSON string.
evidence.limitations: Generated script execution in external Python/browser/Desmos environments was not established by the inspected Rust tests.

evidence.excerpt: CLI initializes a global Rayon pool from --threads/config, clamping nonzero requests to available parallelism and treating zero as all available cores. CPU batch FFT uses par_iter. GPU FFT is initialized with a OnceLock wgpu context and compute pipelines, pads/interpolates data to a power of two, then reads results back; GPU errors warn and fall back to CPU in the facade. Native raster rendering also has a separate cached wgpu render context.
evidence.provenance: CLI, math facade, GPU compute, and emitter/native source.
evidence.limitations: Documentation contains speed estimates, but this record does not treat them as facts: no reproducible benchmark result in the inspected tests establishes general performance or CPU/GPU equivalence.

evidence.excerpt: Config::load uses --config when supplied, otherwise ProjectDirs('vectomancy')/config.toml, parses TOML, and falls back to defaults on absence/read/parse failure. CLI values generally override section values; image defaults include spline mode, PNG image output, terms 1000, detail 50, min path length 5, simplify_math true, and GPU false. Video reads its section and falls back to image for selected fields.
evidence.provenance: Config structs/load code, CLI resolution code, and documentation.
evidence.limitations: Documentation examples include fields at top level that the shown Config struct nests under sections; this record reports code behavior and flags the documentation as a separate claim source rather than reconciling it silently.

evidence.excerpt: Tests reject invalid/no subcommand, run image and text workflows and assert output files, optionally process ten frames when a local video exists, assert a simple TSP ordering, assert FFT term count, assert one spline equation, exercise raster decoding including blank/tiny images, and assert a Chaikin pipeline returns a polyline scene.
evidence.provenance: Test source inspection only; tests were not used as evidence of unmeasured performance or broad correctness.
evidence.limitations: The video test is environment-conditional and uses an absolute local path; passing tests would not establish all video/output cases.

synthesis.statement: Vectomancy has a layered flow: CLI/configuration -> format-specific ingestion -> geometry extraction/normalization -> selectable math transform -> tagged AST -> emitter/native renderer -> optional external video stitching.
synthesis.basis: The named functions and data types connect the stages; this is an architectural reading of local code, not a stated historical design claim.
synthesis.limitations: The repository also exposes workspace pipeline crates and a facade, so this decomposition is a useful projection rather than an exhaustive module graph.

synthesis.statement: The runtime uses two concurrency layers for video: a decoder producer thread and bounded channel, followed by a bounded batch of scoped frame workers; within workers, Rayon may parallelize image/path work, creating deliberate shared-pool oversubscription according to the source comment.
synthesis.basis: The source explicitly creates these scheduling boundaries and comments on the tradeoff.
synthesis.limitations: No independent scheduling trace or benchmark is included.

synthesis.statement: Vectomancy may be a candidate mathematical-neighborhood example for architecture records involving transform pipelines, representation changes, and evidence-bounded approximation controls.
synthesis.basis: The implementation exposes explicit transform modes, intermediate representations, and output contracts.
synthesis.limitations: This is a research hypothesis requiring human review; it is not a typed relation, inclusion decision, or claim that Vectomancy is mathematically equivalent to another system.

synthesis.statement: The AST boundary can be compared by analogy to a compiler-style intermediate representation: ingestion produces structured segments/paths, transforms produce typed variants, and emitters lower them to target formats.
synthesis.basis: Structural resemblance in local data flow.
synthesis.limitations: No historical influence, compiler lineage, semantic equivalence, or relation is asserted.

candidate_relationships.statement: Explore Vectomancy alongside systems that expose explicit approximation/transform pipelines and typed intermediate representations.
